feed.summary: AbbVie has filed a lawsuit against the U.S. government, seeking clearer guidance on patient eligibility for the 340B drug discount program. The company argues that current loopholes allow healthcare providers to claim discounts for patients with minimal contact or even multiple discounts for the same prescription, transforming the program into a revenue stream rather than a safety-net for low-income populations. AbbVie proposes a revised statute where discounts would only apply if the provider directly manages the patient's specific condition and has seen them for a thorough medical visit within the past year.

feed.summary: AbbVie has filed a lawsuit seeking to narrow the eligibility for the 340B drug discount program. feed.title: AbbVie sues to narrow 340B eligibility

feed.summary: AbbVie, the maker of Humira and Botox, has filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration, seeking a narrower definition of an eligible patient for the federal 340B drug discount program. The company argues that the current "overly inclusive" definition allows healthcare providers to claim discounts for patients with only a cursory relationship to the provider. AbbVie proposes limiting eligible patients to those prescribed medication as a direct result of care received within the last 12 months, with the provider actively managing their care.

The study, primarily involving male participants, showed that ABBV-295 was generally well tolerated, with gastrointestinal issues being the most common but mostly mild side effects. Importantly, ABBV-295 demonstrated clinically meaningful, dose-dependent reductions in body weight, ranging from -7.75% to -9.79% at week 12/13 compared to the placebo group.

feed.summary: A federal court in the Middle District of Tennessee denied AbbVie's motion for a preliminary injunction, rejecting its challenge to a state law that prohibits pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) from preventing pharmacies from participating in preferred networks based on their chosen contract pharmacy arrangements.
